text: In recognition of World Cities Day, @NationMediaGrp (NMG), is partnering with the Architectural Association of Kenya (AAK), to host a forum on 29th and 30th October at the Iconic Plaza Hotel, Nairobi, under the theme “From Urban Challenges to Smart, Sustainable and Inclusive Futures.” The two-day forum will bring together built environment professionals, industry leaders and innovators for exhibitions, thought-leadership sessions, masterclasses and networking opportunities focused on the future of our cities. Be part of the conversation: For registration and partnership enquiries, contact: Nation Media Group Jason: +254 719 852 358 jjmutua@ke.nationmedia.com Architectural Association of Kenya (AAK) +254 721 691 337 aak@aak.or.ke

text: Working with registered, licensed professionals and maintaining site instruction books creates clear communication channels. When issues arise, this documentation makes it easy to trace responsibility and place accountability on the right individual.

Many buildings lack adequate natural light, ventilation, and essential infrastructure, potentially compromising occupants’ health, comfort, and productivity. The Healthy Homes Guidelines and Checklist (HHGC) provides a practical resource to help tenants and prospective homeowners assess key indicators of a healthy living environment, including natural lighting, ventilation, and access to essential services, before renting or purchasing a home. Read the guidelines here: aak.or.ke/initiatives/healthy-homes-guidelines

Public awareness empowers citizens to demand quality construction and identify potentially unsafe developments. Through initiatives such as Je, Una Mjengo? and reporting platforms such as Mulika Mjengo, the public can flag and report concerns, including construction sites without mandatory project site boards or missing consultant details, so that such issues are escalated before disasters occur. Report an unsafe construction site here: aak.or.ke/initiatives/mulika-mjengo
